properties.natural_language: The Fulu fork transition must only occur at an epoch boundary where slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0 AND compute_epoch_at_slot(slot) == FULU_FORK_EPOCH (411392).

reachability.notes: If the fork condition check is incorrect, nodes could fork at different epochs, causing a network split. This is an internal logic bug, not directly attacker-triggered.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect fork activation epoch would split the entire network into incompatible chains.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: A bug here would cause a consensus failure affecting all nodes.

properties.natural_language: After upgrade_to_fulu() completes, fork.previous_version must equal the Electra fork version, fork.current_version must equal FULU_FORK_VERSION (0x06000000), and fork.epoch must equal the current epoch.

reachability.notes: Incorrect fork version fields would cause nodes to disagree on the active fork, leading to consensus failures.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong fork version would cause all nodes running the buggy client to split from the network.

properties.natural_language: After upgrade_to_fulu() completes, the proposer_lookahead array must be initialized with (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH valid proposer indices.

reachability.notes: If proposer lookahead is incorrectly initialized at fork, nodes will disagree on proposer assignments for subsequent slots.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect proposer lookahead initialization would cause consensus disagreements across all nodes running the buggy client.

properties.natural_language: All Electra state fields (validators, balances, participation flags, sync committees, pending operations) must be preserved unchanged through the Fulu fork transition.

reachability.notes: State corruption during fork transition would cause validator balances or other critical data to be lost or altered.

properties.severity_justification: State corruption during fork could affect all validator balances and participation records network-wide.

properties.natural_language: The fork transition must only occur when the slot is at an epoch boundary (slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0). If this condition is not met, the fork must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Fork at a non-epoch boundary would corrupt state transition logic.

properties.severity_justification: Fork at wrong slot would corrupt state for all nodes running the buggy client (>33% if single client).

properties.natural_language: Nodes syncing past the fork epoch must apply upgrade_to_fulu retroactively at the correct epoch boundary during state replay, producing the same post-fork state as nodes that were live during the transition.

reachability.notes: Syncing nodes that miss the fork epoch must still produce identical states. Failure would cause newly synced nodes to fork.

properties.severity_justification: Syncing nodes producing different states would be unable to follow the canonical chain, affecting >33% of newly joining nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Derived from ambiguity AMB-FULU-FORK-01 about missing sync behavior spec.

properties.natural_language: For genesis networks, fork.previous_version must be set to FULU_FORK_VERSION (same as current_version) when there is no prior fork.

reachability.notes: Only relevant for genesis networks (testnets). Mainnet always has a prior fork.

properties.severity_justification: Only affects genesis networks (testnets), not mainnet.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Derived from ambiguity AMB-FULU-FORK-02. Testnet-only impact.

properties.natural_language: The proposer_lookahead vector length must always equal (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH after initialization and after each epoch boundary processing.

reachability.notes: Wrong vector length would cause out-of-bounds access or missing proposer assignments.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect vector length would crash or produce wrong proposer assignments for all nodes with the bug.

properties.natural_language: After proposer lookahead initialization, each entry in the proposer_lookahead vector must reference a valid, active validator index for the corresponding slot's epoch.

reachability.notes: Invalid proposer index would cause block proposals to fail or be rejected.

properties.severity_justification: Invalid proposer indices would cause missed slots and attestation failures for affected nodes.

properties.natural_language: At each epoch boundary, process_proposer_lookahead must shift the lookahead window by exactly one epoch: removing the earliest epoch's SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries and appending SLOTS_PER_EPOCH new entries for current_epoch + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1.

reachability.notes: Incorrect window shift would cause stale or misaligned proposer assignments.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect window shift would cause all nodes with the bug to disagree on proposer assignments (>33% if single client).

properties.natural_language: After process_proposer_lookahead completes, get_beacon_proposer_index must return the value at state.proposer_lookahead[state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH] without any on-demand calculation.

reachability.notes: If get_beacon_proposer_index does not use the pre-computed value, proposer assignments could diverge.

properties.severity_justification: Divergent proposer index computation would cause consensus disagreement.

properties.natural_language: Before computing proposer indices for a future epoch, the RANDAO seed for DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER for that epoch must be available and finalized in the beacon state.

reachability.notes: Using an unavailable or stale RANDAO mix would produce incorrect proposer assignments.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong seed would cause all nodes with the bug to compute different proposers.

properties.natural_language: Before computing proposer indices, the set of active validators for the target epoch must be correctly derived from the beacon state.

reachability.notes: Wrong active validator set would produce incorrect proposer selection.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect validator set for proposer selection would cause consensus disagreement.

properties.natural_language: get_blob_parameters must always return valid BlobParameters for any epoch >= ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH, falling back to Electra-era defaults if no BLOB_SCHEDULE entry matches.

reachability.notes: If get_blob_parameters returns no result or incorrect parameters, block validation would fail or accept invalid blocks.

properties.severity_justification: Missing or wrong blob parameters would cause nodes to reject valid blocks or accept invalid ones, splitting the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Derived from ambiguity AMB-FULU-BEACON-01 about unspecified fallback values.

properties.natural_language: The BLOB_SCHEDULE entries must be sorted in ascending epoch order. The descending iteration in get_blob_parameters depends on this ordering for correctness.

reachability.notes: Unsorted blob schedule is a configuration error. The spec says 'should' not 'must' for sorting, creating ambiguity.

properties.severity_justification: Unsorted schedule could cause incorrect parameter resolution for >5% of nodes with misconfigured clients.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Configuration-dependent. Derived from ambiguity AMB-FULU-BEACON-02.

properties.natural_language: Before validating blob commitments in a block, the blob parameters for the current epoch must be resolved via get_blob_parameters. The resolved max_blobs_per_block must be a positive integer.

reachability.notes: If max_blobs_per_block is 0 or negative, all blocks would be rejected or all accepted regardless of blob count.

properties.severity_justification: Zero or negative max_blobs would cause all blob-carrying blocks to be rejected, halting rollup data availability.

properties.natural_language: After blob commitment validation, a block is accepted only if len(body.blob_kzg_commitments) <= resolved max_blobs_per_block. Blocks exceeding the limit must be rejected.

reachability.notes: An attacker-proposed block with excessive blob commitments must be rejected. Failure to reject could cause state bloat.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting blocks with excessive blobs would cause state bloat and consensus disagreement with correct nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Attacker can propose blocks with excessive blob commitments via P2P gossip.

properties.natural_language: All nodes must agree on the BLOB_SCHEDULE configuration. There is no on-chain mechanism to validate the schedule; divergent configurations will cause network partitioning.

reachability.notes: Configuration disagreement is operator error, but could be exploited if a client ships with wrong defaults.

properties.severity_justification: Divergent blob schedules would split the network. If a client ships wrong defaults, all nodes running that client fork off.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Configuration-dependent. However, if a client implementation has wrong default BLOB_SCHEDULE, this becomes an internal-bug.

properties.natural_language: After compute_fork_digest completes, the result must be the XOR of the base fork digest (from fork version + genesis validators root) and the truncated-to-4-bytes hash of (epoch || max_blobs_per_block).

reachability.notes: Incorrect fork digest computation would cause nodes to connect to wrong peers or reject correct peers.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong fork digest would partition all nodes running the buggy client from the rest of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Derived from ambiguity AMB-FULU-BEACON-04 about hash truncation.

properties.natural_language: A remote peer's fork digest must match the local node's computed fork digest (including blob parameter hash) before the peer connection is accepted.

reachability.notes: An attacker could attempt to connect with a crafted fork digest to infiltrate or partition the network.

properties.severity_justification: Failure to reject mismatched fork digests could allow network partition attacks affecting >33% of nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Maps to boundary edge EDGE-REMOTE-PEER-FORK-DIGEST from trust model.

properties.natural_language: Nodes with identical fork version, genesis validators root, and blob schedule must compute identical fork digests. Nodes with different blob parameters must compute different fork digests.

reachability.notes: If XOR + truncation produces collisions for different blob params, incompatible nodes could connect.

properties.severity_justification: Fork digest collision would allow incompatible peers to exchange blocks, causing validation failures.

properties.natural_language: Before accepting a beacon block received from a P2P peer, the blob_kzg_commitments count must be validated against get_blob_parameters(get_current_epoch(state)).max_blobs_per_block.

reachability.notes: Attacker can send blocks via P2P gossip with any number of blob commitments. Validation must enforce the dynamic limit.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing blob commitment limits could cause state divergence between correct and buggy nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Maps to boundary edge EDGE-PEER-BLOCK-TO-CL-VALIDATION from trust model.

properties.natural_language: The execution payload must be verified via the Engine API (execution layer client) before the block is considered valid.

reachability.notes: Skipping EL verification would allow invalid execution payloads to be accepted.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting blocks without EL verification could lead to invalid state transitions affecting all nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Maps to boundary edge EDGE-EL-PAYLOAD-VERIFICATION from trust model.

properties.natural_language: After execution payload processing, if blob commitment count exceeds the dynamic limit, the block must be in STATE-PAYLOAD-REJECTED. If within limit and EL verification passes, block must be in STATE-PAYLOAD-VALID.

reachability.notes: Correct rejection of over-limit blocks is critical for consensus.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect accept/reject decision on blob limits causes consensus split.

properties.natural_language: The epoch processing pipeline must execute in the correct order: justification/finalization → rewards/penalties → sync committee updates → proposer lookahead. The proposer lookahead step must always be the final step.

reachability.notes: Incorrect ordering would cause proposer lookahead to use wrong state (e.g., pre-rewards validator set).

properties.severity_justification: Wrong epoch processing order would produce different states on all nodes running the buggy client.

properties.natural_language: After epoch processing completes, the proposer_lookahead vector must contain updated proposer indices for the new lookahead window covering current_epoch through current_epoch + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1.

reachability.notes: Stale proposer lookahead after epoch processing would cause incorrect proposer assignments.

properties.severity_justification: Stale lookahead after epoch processing would cause missed slots and consensus disagreement.

properties.natural_language: The proposer_lookahead vector must be fully populated before it is queried. At the Fulu fork activation epoch, it must be initialized before any slot processing occurs.

reachability.notes: Querying an uninitialized lookahead would cause a crash or return garbage proposer indices.

properties.severity_justification: Uninitialized lookahead query at fork activation would crash all nodes running the buggy client.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Derived from ambiguity AMB-FULU-BEACON-03 about unspecified initialization behavior.

properties.natural_language: The deterministic proposer lookahead reveals future proposers MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1 epochs in advance. This advance knowledge must not enable proposer-targeted attacks that were not possible before EIP-7917.

reachability.notes: Advance knowledge of proposers could enable targeted DoS attacks against specific validators.

properties.severity_justification: Targeted proposer DoS could affect >5% of slots if attacker can identify and attack proposers in advance.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires analysis of whether advance proposer knowledge creates new attack vectors vs pre-EIP-7917.

properties.natural_language: All client implementations must update their BLOB_SCHEDULE configuration in sync with scheduled epoch changes. Clients that miss an update will reject valid blocks or accept invalid ones after the scheduled epoch.

reachability.notes: No protocol-level enforcement of blob schedule updates. Relies on client teams shipping correct updates.

properties.severity_justification: Missed update by a major client would fork all nodes running that client (potentially >33%).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Configuration-dependent, but could be critical if client defaults are wrong.

properties.natural_language: The blob base fee must never fall below the reserve price floor defined by BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee_per_gas / GAS_PER_BLOB. When blob fee is below this threshold, the reserve pricing mode must be active.

reachability.notes: Incorrect reserve price comparison would cause wrong pricing mode selection, affecting fee calculations.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong pricing mode would produce different excess_blob_gas values, causing consensus split between correct and buggy nodes.

properties.natural_language: The reserve price condition check must use the correct comparison: BLOB_BASE_COST * parent.base_fee_per_gas > GAS_PER_BLOB * get_blob_basefee(parent_header). The comparison must use integer arithmetic without overflow.

reachability.notes: Integer overflow in the multiplication could cause incorrect mode selection. BLOB_BASE_COST (2^13) * base_fee could overflow in some implementations.

properties.severity_justification: Arithmetic overflow causing wrong mode selection would affect consensus for all blocks, splitting the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Integer overflow risk in BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee multiplication.

properties.natural_language: When reserve condition is true, calc_excess_blob_gas must compute: excess += blob_gas_used * (max - target) / max. When false, it must compute: excess += blob_gas_used - target_blob_gas (standard formula).

reachability.notes: Wrong formula application would produce incorrect excess_blob_gas, causing block validation failures.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong excess_blob_gas computation is consensus-critical; all nodes must agree on the value for every block.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Derived from ambiguity AMB-EIP7918-02 about abbreviated parameter names.

properties.natural_language: The 'max' and 'target' values used in the reserve mode formula must be MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK and TARGET_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK from the EIP-7840 blobSchedule for the current fork.

reachability.notes: Using wrong max/target parameters would produce incorrect excess calculations.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong parameters in the formula would cause all blocks to have incorrect excess_blob_gas, splitting the network.

properties.natural_language: At fork activation, new blobSchedule parameters must be applied immediately starting from the first block at or after the fork timestamp. No transition period is allowed.

reachability.notes: Delayed parameter application would cause blocks at the fork boundary to be computed with wrong parameters.

properties.severity_justification: Using old parameters after fork activation would cause consensus split for all blocks at the fork boundary.

properties.natural_language: When validating a block received from a P2P peer, the excess_blob_gas header field must be recalculated using the modified calc_excess_blob_gas (with reserve price logic) and compared to the header value.

reachability.notes: Attacker can send blocks via P2P with arbitrary excess_blob_gas values. Validation must recalculate and compare.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting blocks with wrong excess_blob_gas would cause fee calculation divergence, potentially affecting >33% of nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Maps to boundary edge EDGE-PEER-BLOCK-TO-EL-VALIDATION from trust model.

properties.natural_language: After block validation, if the recalculated excess_blob_gas matches the header value, the block is valid. If they differ, the block must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Attacker can craft blocks with mismatched excess_blob_gas. Must be deterministically rejected.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting blocks with wrong excess_blob_gas leads to fee divergence and consensus split.

properties.natural_language: The reserve price condition must be evaluated every block. Transitions between normal and reserve pricing modes must be smooth with no discontinuities in the excess_blob_gas trajectory.

reachability.notes: Skipping the reserve check on some blocks would produce incorrect excess values.

properties.severity_justification: Inconsistent mode evaluation would cause non-deterministic excess_blob_gas across blocks.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Derived from ambiguity AMB-EIP7918-01.

properties.natural_language: BLOB_BASE_COST must equal 2^13 (8192). GAS_PER_BLOB must equal 2^17 (131072). The ratio BLOB_BASE_COST / GAS_PER_BLOB = 1/16 defines the minimum reserve ratio between blob and execution costs.

reachability.notes: Wrong constant values would cause incorrect reserve price calculations across all blocks.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong constants would affect fee calculations for every block, causing immediate consensus split.

properties.natural_language: All client implementations must use identical logic for the reserve price condition check and the two excess calculation formulas. Any implementation difference causes consensus failure.

reachability.notes: Implementation differences in integer division, rounding, or overflow handling would cause consensus failures.

properties.severity_justification: Implementation divergence in consensus-critical calculations splits the network along client boundaries.

properties.natural_language: Attackers must not be able to manipulate execution gas prices to artificially inflate or deflate blob costs via the reserve price mechanism. The linkage between execution and blob fees must not create profitable manipulation strategies.

reachability.notes: Attacker could submit transactions to manipulate base_fee_per_gas, indirectly affecting blob pricing via the reserve mechanism.

properties.severity_justification: Economic manipulation of blob fees could destabilize rollup economics but would not crash nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires economic analysis of manipulation costs vs profits.

properties.natural_language: The proposer identity of a received block must be verified against the proposer_lookahead vector before the block is accepted. The proposer signature must be valid.

reachability.notes: Attacker could send blocks claiming to be from a different proposer. Lookahead verification prevents this.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting blocks from unauthorized proposers would cause consensus disagreement.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Maps to boundary edge EDGE-PROPOSER-BLOCK-SUBMISSION from trust model.

properties.natural_language: When validating a block received via Engine API from the CL, the EL must recalculate excess_blob_gas using the modified calc_excess_blob_gas with reserve price logic, independently of the CL's calculation.

reachability.notes: Engine API is semi-trusted. EL must independently validate even data from the CL. A buggy CL could send wrong payloads.

properties.severity_justification: Trusting CL's excess_blob_gas without recalculation could propagate errors from buggy CL implementations.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Maps to boundary edge EDGE-CL-PAYLOAD-TO-EL from trust model.

properties.natural_language: After the fork digest is computed and advertised, peers with matching fork digests must be connected and peers with mismatched digests must be rejected. No peer connection should be established without fork digest verification.

reachability.notes: Attacker could bypass fork digest check to connect incompatible peers.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing fork digest verification enables network partition attacks.

properties.natural_language: In reserve mode, the excess blob gas calculation uses blob_gas_used * (max - target) / max, which always produces a non-negative value (no subtraction from excess). This prevents excess from decreasing when in reserve mode.

reachability.notes: If max < target (which should never happen), the formula produces negative values. Underflow protection needed.

properties.severity_justification: Underflow in reserve mode calculation would produce wildly incorrect excess values.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Edge case: what happens if max_blob_gas <= target_blob_gas due to misconfiguration?

properties.natural_language: The RANDAO mixes used for proposer seed computation must be finalized and identical across all nodes at the time process_proposer_lookahead runs.

reachability.notes: Validators can manipulate RANDAO reveals to bias proposer selection. MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD mitigates this but the window is small.

properties.severity_justification: RANDAO manipulation to bias proposer selection could affect >5% of slots under certain conditions.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Pre-existing RANDAO manipulation risk, but EIP-7917 changes the impact by making assignments visible earlier.

properties.natural_language: The proposer lookahead step in epoch processing must occur after all other epoch processing steps (justification, rewards, slashings, sync committees) to ensure it uses the final updated state.

reachability.notes: Computing lookahead before rewards/slashings would use a different active validator set than intended.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong ordering would produce different proposer assignments on all nodes with the bug.

properties.natural_language: The excess_blob_gas value must be monotonically non-decreasing when in reserve mode (since the formula only adds). In normal mode, it may decrease when blob_gas_used < target_blob_gas.

reachability.notes: Violations of this monotonicity in reserve mode indicate implementation bugs.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect monotonicity behavior indicates a formula bug that would cause consensus divergence.

properties.natural_language: All nodes in the network must agree on FULU_FORK_EPOCH = 411392. Nodes activating at different epochs would create incompatible chains.

reachability.notes: If a client ships with wrong FULU_FORK_EPOCH, all nodes running that client would fork at the wrong epoch.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong fork epoch constant would split all nodes of that client from the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Configuration constant. If shipped wrong by a client, it becomes an internal-bug.

properties.natural_language: Blocks received from P2P peers must have their blob_kzg_commitments count validated against the dynamic limit from get_blob_parameters for the block's epoch, not a hardcoded constant.

reachability.notes: Using a hardcoded limit instead of the dynamic blob schedule would cause rejection of valid blocks after blob parameter updates.

properties.severity_justification: Hardcoded blob limit would cause block rejection divergence after blob schedule changes.

properties.natural_language: The block producer must correctly determine whether reserve or normal pricing mode applies before computing the excess_blob_gas for the block header.

validation_layers: Block header validation by receiving nodes
reachability.notes: A malicious block producer could compute excess_blob_gas with the wrong mode. Receiving nodes must independently verify.

properties.severity_justification: Block with incorrectly calculated excess_blob_gas would be rejected by correct nodes, causing proposer penalties.

properties.natural_language: The fork activation timestamp must be correctly identified. The first block at or after the fork timestamp must use the new blobSchedule parameters for all calculations.

reachability.notes: Off-by-one in fork activation could cause one block to use wrong parameters.

properties.severity_justification: Off-by-one at fork boundary would cause consensus split for the fork activation block.

properties.natural_language: The proposer lookahead computation must be deterministic: given the same beacon state, all implementations must produce the identical proposer_lookahead vector.

reachability.notes: Non-deterministic proposer computation (e.g., hash function differences) would cause cross-client consensus failures.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic proposer computation would cause cross-client consensus failures.

properties.natural_language: After compute_fork_digest with blob parameters, the fork digest must incorporate both the fork version and the active blob parameters. Changes to blob parameters must produce a different fork digest.

reachability.notes: If blob parameter changes don't affect fork digest, peers on different schedules could connect.

properties.severity_justification: Unchanged fork digest after blob param change would allow incompatible peers to exchange invalid blocks.

properties.natural_language: The parent block's base_fee_per_gas, excess_blob_gas, and blob_gas_used must be available and correctly read before computing the reserve price condition and excess blob gas.

reachability.notes: Reading wrong parent data (e.g., from uncle blocks) would produce incorrect excess calculations.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong parent data produces incorrect fee calculations for all subsequent blocks.

properties.natural_language: After the Fulu fork transition completes, the beacon chain must be operating under Fulu fork rules with all new state fields (including proposer_lookahead) initialized. No pre-Fulu state processing rules should apply.

reachability.notes: Lingering pre-Fulu rules after fork activation would cause inconsistent block processing.

properties.severity_justification: Incomplete fork activation would cause all blocks after the fork to be processed incorrectly.
